title: Quick Tip: Say Goodbye to OData on Microsoft Pages in Business Central 2027 Wave 1 (version 30.0)
summary: Starting with Business Central version 30.0 (2027 Wave 1), Microsoft no longer allows exposing Microsoft-authored pages as OData endpoints. Developers using UI pages for integrations must migrate to custom extensions, query objects, or purpose-built APIs to maintain connectivity and ensure long-term stability.
key_points: Microsoft-authored pages from Base Application and System Application cannot be exposed as OData endpoints in version 30.0
UI pages are designed for human interaction and change between releases, making them unsuitable for stable integrations
Developers must audit current integrations, migrate to custom extensions or query objects, and design purpose-built APIs
This change enforces separation between user interface and API layers for more robust and predictable integrations

quotes.text: UI pages are designed for human interaction - not for stable, long-term integration. They can change between releases without warning.
quotes.why_it_matters: Explains why exposing pages as OData endpoints is fragile and leads to broken integrations with new releases

quotes.text: You cannot expose any Microsoft-authored page from apps like Base Application, System Application, or other first-party apps as an OData endpoint.
quotes.why_it_matters: States the core enforcement rule in version 30.0 that developers must prepare for

quotes.text: This change is part of a broader effort to make Business Central integrations more robust, predictable, and future-proof.
quotes.why_it_matters: Clarifies Microsoft's intent to improve integration stability by enforcing clear separation between UI and API layers
